slides.title: Buterin and Durov both place privacy in core infrastructure
paragraphs: Buterin and Durov both place privacy in core infrastructure
The founders of Ethereum and Telegram, a messaging app with over a billion monthly users, reach the same conclusion from different starting points.
Vitalik Buterin
Co-founder
Ethereum
“Privacy is not about standing apart. It’s about standing together.” Why I support privacy, 14 April 2025
Why it matters
Control over information is power, so privacy protects decentralisation, personal freedom and institutions such as the secret ballot.
Where it belongs
Privacy belongs in the protocol, covering payments, application activity, chain reads and network-level anonymity.
Current gap
Much of the proposal remains a roadmap that wallets and applications would need to implement.
Pavel Durov
Founder and CEO
Telegram, over 1B monthly users
“Telegram would rather exit a market than undermine encryption with backdoors and violate basic human rights.” Telegram channel, 21 April 2025
Why it matters
Encryption protects everyday communication and personal safety, and any access built for authorities is also available to attackers.
Where it belongs
The product should exclude backdoors, even if that means withdrawing from a market.
Current gap
Telegram’s default Cloud Chats are not end-to-end encrypted; only Secret Chats are.
Implication Both argue for privacy in systems people already use, making wallet and application adoption central to how widely it reaches users.

details.label: 31 months under sanctions
details.description: Tornado Cash stayed on the US sanctions list from 8 August 2022 until 21 March 2025. For that period any US person who used it risked breaking sanctions law, which pushed developers and companies away from on-chain privacy tools.
details.source: US Treasury; Van Loon v. Treasury

details.label: US Treasury sanctions Tornado Cash
details.description: Tornado Cash is an Ethereum mixer: users deposit into a shared pool and withdraw to a fresh address, breaking the public link between sender and recipient. On 8 August 2022 the US Treasury’s sanctions office (OFAC) blacklisted its smart contracts, saying it had laundered more than $7B since 2019, including $455M stolen by North Korea’s Lazarus Group.

details.label: Court rules code is not property
details.description: In Van Loon v. Department of the Treasury, decided 26 November 2024, the Fifth Circuit appeals court held that Tornado Cash’s immutable smart contracts are not property that can be sanctioned, because nobody owns or controls them. It was the first appellate ruling to put ownerless privacy code outside sanctions law.
details.source: US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, 26 November 2024

details.label: US Treasury lifts the sanctions
details.description: The US Treasury removed Tornado Cash from the sanctions list on 21 March 2025, so US users could interact with it again. Developer liability is still open: in August 2025 a jury convicted developer Roman Storm of conspiring to run an unlicensed money-transmitting business and deadlocked on laundering and sanctions charges, which face retrial on 26 April 2027.

details.label: Buterin and Durov
details.description: On 11 April 2025 Buterin proposed making privacy part of Ethereum’s core design, covering payments, app activity, chain reads and network-level anonymity. On 21 April Durov said Telegram would leave a market rather than build encryption backdoors for authorities. Two founders with very large user bases put privacy at the centre of their products.
details.source: Buterin, 11 April 2025; Durov’s Telegram channel, 21 April 2025

details.label: GENIUS Act
details.description: The Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act, signed on 18 July 2025, is the first US federal law for payment stablecoins, setting rules for reserves, licensing and redemption. It gives banks and payment companies a legal route onto public chains, bringing payroll and supplier flows that companies normally keep confidential.

details.label: USAD and the Privacy Cluster
details.description: On 1 October 2025 Paxos Labs and Aleo announced USAD, a US dollar stablecoin whose balances and transfers are private by default. On 9 October the Ethereum Foundation formed a Privacy Cluster of 47 researchers, engineers and cryptographers to make privacy a first-class property of Ethereum.
details.source: Paxos Labs and Aleo, 1 October 2025; The Block, 9 October 2025

details.label: a16z: privacy is crypto’s moat
details.description: a16z crypto’s Ali Yahya argued that privacy will be the strongest moat for blockchains: “bridging tokens is easy, bridging secrets is hard”. A chain that holds users’ private state is harder to leave than one that holds only public balances, which favours privacy networks that gain users early.

details.label: Grayscale’s Zcash ETF lists
details.description: Grayscale’s Zcash ETF (ZCSH) began trading on NYSE Arca on 25 August 2026 and held $463.2M by 7 September, giving investors with ordinary brokerage accounts regulated exposure to a privacy coin.
details.source: Grayscale; NYSE Arca, 25 August to 7 September 2026

Stablecoin supply exceeds crypto ETFs, DeFi and tokenised assets combined, exposing payment flows and counterparty relationships on public ledgers.
Public payments can reveal a company’s counterparties, payment amounts and treasury balances.
Tether and Circle account for 84% of supply; their public transfers can be monitored.
Public payroll and supplier payments can expose information companies normally keep confidential.

slides.title: Privacy demand alone does not set token value
paragraphs: Privacy demand alone does not set token value
Investors value privacy most when it is held as money: Zcash and Monero are worth about $31B together, and Venice reaches $1.1B because customer revenue buys back its token.

Grass and Helium, at $486M and $85M, show what networks that sell bandwidth and coverage can be worth once customers pay, which makes them reference points for UR (SN25) without setting its fair value.
Nym and UR (SN25), which hide who is talking to whom, are worth $30.6M combined, about 1,000 times less than transaction privacy, even though wallet privacy can fail at the network connection.

slides.title: Aztec’s private rollup is live, but $12M of stake secures only $58K of user funds
paragraphs: Aztec’s private rollup is live, but $12M of stake secures only $58K of user funds

Each transaction is proved on the user’s device and settled on Ethereum by staked sequencers and provers, so AZTEC is needed both to operate the network and to pay its fees, yet only $58K of user funds have arrived and v5 carries a critical proving bug disclosed on 7 August.
What it sells Private smart contracts on Ethereum. Apps written in Noir can keep balances, logic and state hidden while still calling public contracts, so one app can mix private and public steps.

How value reaches the token Users must convert AZTEC into Fee Juice to transact, and the congestion share of each fee is burned. Each sequencer seat needs 200,000 AZTEC, so more usage and more operators both pull on the token.

What has to be true v6 must fix the critical proving bug disclosed on 7 August, which L2BEAT says puts funds and contract state at risk, and apps must bring user funds far above $58K for fees to matter next to rewards.

Supply risk Only 29% of the 10.35B supply circulates, the Foundation unlocks on 13 November, governance can mint up to 20% of supply a year, and rewards of 400 AZTEC per slot add to circulating supply.

details.label: Your device
details.description: The Private Execution Environment (PXE) in the user’s wallet runs private functions locally and proves they ran correctly with a zero-knowledge proof. Only the proof, new note commitments and nullifiers leave the device.

details.label: Sequencers
details.description: Each epoch a 48-member committee is sampled from the staked sequencer set. Sequencers check the private proofs, run any public functions and propose blocks. Joining the set requires 200,000 AZTEC.

details.label: Provers
details.description: Proving is permissionless. Provers produce one validity proof for an epoch of blocks and post it to Ethereum, earning 30% of block rewards and of unburned fees.

details.label: Ethereum settlement
details.description: A verifier contract on Ethereum checks each epoch proof. Once it verifies, the state change is final and inherits Ethereum’s security.

details.label: What observers can see
details.description: Aztec documentation says the only information a private transaction leaks is how many private state updates it makes and which public functions it calls. Senders, recipients, amounts and private calls stay hidden.

details.label: Fees
details.description: Fees are paid in Fee Juice, created by depositing AZTEC one-for-one; it cannot be bridged back. Each fee is mana used times the mana price. The congestion part of each fee is burned, and the rest goes 70% to the sequencer and 30% to provers.

details.label: Rewards
details.description: The current checkpoint reward is 400 AZTEC per slot, split 280 to sequencers and 120 to provers, and governance can change it. Rewards are minted in advance to a distributor contract, so they add to circulating supply.

slides.title: Umbra’s fees reach a treasury that UMBRA holders govern, with no automatic payout
paragraphs: Umbra’s fees reach a treasury that UMBRA holders govern, with no automatic payout

Umbra hides who paid whom, and how much, on Solana, and each private transaction pays a protocol fee into a treasury that only a governance vote can direct, so UMBRA holders decide how fee income is spent but receive none of it automatically.

What it sells A private wallet for Solana that hides sender, recipient and amount on transfers and the size of swaps. It opened to the public in March 2026 with viewing keys, risk screening and geo-blocking for compliance.

How value reaches the token Fees go to a treasury account that only a timelocked vote can set, and UMBRA holders steer it through MetaDAO markets. There is no automatic buyback or dividend, so value depends on how the DAO spends.

Why the vesting matters Team and adviser tokens unlock only when fully diluted value reaches 2×, 4×, 8×, 16× and 32× the $0.30 sale price, so insider supply arrives only after the price has multiplied.

What has to be true Nimbus, the shielded pool Umbra is building for other apps, has to launch and lift deposits well beyond $187K, because treasury income grows only with the value moving through the pool.

paragraphs: Venice turns AI revenue into VVV burns while cutting issuance to 2M a year

Customers pay for private AI through subscriptions, purchased credits or staked DIEM, part of that spending buys and burns VVV, and holders stake VVV to earn emissions and mint DIEM for daily API credit.

What it sells Private AI chat, images and API access to open-source and third-party models. Venice says it does not store prompts or replies, and users pick per model between private, anonymised, TEE and encrypted modes.

How value reaches the token Staked VVV earns emissions and can be locked to mint DIEM, each worth $1 of API use a day when staked. Since 17 July 2026, $5 of every $100 of credits bought has bought and burned VVV, alongside subscription burns.
Evidence of demand 3.5M registered users and a $100M annualised revenue run rate (company-reported, August 2026), after a $65M Series A at a $1B valuation led by Dragonfly.

What has to be true Burns need to outpace the 2M VVV still issued each year. API calls paid with DIEM are not credit purchases, so the burn depends on paid credits and subscriptions continuing to grow.
